record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code and artifact contents were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports an upstream replication using difference-in-means directions and ablation, with results on refusal behavior. The reported safety ablation is not the full all-layer/all-position intervention in the claim.
record.gate_note: Rows use only outcomes stated in the README. Listed artifacts are not treated as evidence beyond results the README explicitly reports. The README also reports geometry between safety and epistemic directions, but that does not test whether safety refusal is mediated by one direction. Capability-refusal and refusal-overlap results are not included as evidence about safety refusal.
record.test_reason: It extracts a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction (AdvBench vs Alpaca) in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, ablates it, and measures harmful-request refusal. The upstream replication and the safety-QLoRA checkpoint C both report refusal outcomes. The intervention differs from the original: a top-1 layer ablation at strength 1.5 (L22 in the extension setup), not all-layer/all-position projection. There is also no addition test.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, with one addition. The authors conclude that safety fine-tuning reorganizes refusal representations and causal effects rather than amplifying one fixed direction. They also conclude that safety and epistemic directions are separate. They further conclude that capability refusal is a distinct but partially safety-aligned mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes difference-in-means extraction and direction ablation, but does not report the claim's all-layer/all-position ablation or an addition intervention. This is a fork with an upstream replication pipeline and additional capability-refusal and fine-tuning experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The safety direction used for ablation matters in the tuned checkpoint: the original B direction has essentially no effect, while the new C direction reduces refusal.

fits_no_version.finding: Safety-refusal and epistemic-abstention directions are near-orthogonal: mean cosine 0.049, max 0.183 at layer 20 in Llama-3.1-8B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different abstention behaviours (safety refusal vs. 'I don't know') use separate directions.

fits_no_version.finding: The capability-refusal direction has cosine ≈0.20 with safety across Llama, Qwen and Gemma. Its own ablation cuts capability refusal 13.3pp (p=0.0078). Safety-direction ablation cuts it 8.3pp (p=0.125, not significant). In C, the C capability direction reduces capability refusal from 0.967 to 0.000.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal for lack of capability is a distinct, partially safety-aligned direction.

record.peer_reviewed: ICML 2026 Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop poster for the upstream work; the README says the capability-refusal extension has no separate paper or preprint.
record.problems: The available text is a README and file list, not a full paper or run of the code. The safety-ablation results lack rates and uncertainty estimates; the C ablation result lacks a post-ablation rate. The fine-tuning comparison reports one controlled QLoRA setting.
record.rows_left_out: No results were inferred from named artifact files. The README's capability-refusal and refusal-overlap sections do not report results that directly measure the safety-refusal direction claim; the safety-versus-epistemic cosine and probe results likewise do not test whether safety refusal itself has one mediating direction.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal; all-layer/all-position ablation; preservation of general capabilities (only epistemic abstention stability is mentioned).
Transfer across languages and from base to instruct models; only transfer from the instruct model to its own safety-QLoRA variant is tested.
Whether training method or timing determines that a single removable direction exists; the one QLoRA run leaves a removable direction in place.
Not tested: no weight edits or released abliterated models.
Not tested: no jailbreaks or adversarial training.
Not tested: safety refusal's own dimensionality is not examined.
Not tested: harmfulness judgment versus refusal is not separated.
Not tested: no reasoning models (Qwen3-8B is used only for geometry).

missing.what: Cross-family safety-direction replication (Qwen3-8B, Gemma-2-9B) described only as 'qualitatively consistent'; no ablation rates given.
Baseline harmful refusal for B (0.950) and benign refusal B 0.000 vs C 0.045, giving context for r2/r3.
Numerical upstream cross-ablation sweep for the safety direction (rates and bootstrap CIs) exists in artifacts but not in the README.

record.verdict_notes: The source is a README only, with no paper text, so the evidence is self-reported and the upstream ablation has no numbers. I reassigned r2 and r4 from V1/V7 to V6, since they test whether the direction carries from one model variant to another. V7 is dropped because the fine-tuned model still has a single removable direction. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not report adding the direction, removing it from every layer and position, or measuring preservation of general capabilities.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration results are reported.
No jailbreak suppression of the direction or training against its ablation is reported.
The reported safety-versus-epistemic direction comparison does not test whether safety refusal itself is affine, conical, or composed of multiple directions.
No separation between harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is tested.
No language transfer, base-to-instruct transfer, or direction transfer between model variants is reported.
The README reports one controlled safety QLoRA fine-tuning comparison; it does not test other training methods, schedules, or training stages.
